content: 1. The 2nd Biannual Conference of the Italian SIGCHI Chapter was held in New York and published by the Association for Computing Machinery in 2017, covering pages 1 to 5. 2. The report titled Managing Climate Extremes and Disasters in the Health Sector: Lessons from the IPCC SREX Report was accessed on February 2, 2021, in PDF format. 3. Marchigiani R, Gordy S, Cipolla J, Adams RC, Evans DC, Stehly C, and colleagues conducted a comprehensive review of current management strategies for wind disasters, published in the International Journal of Critical Illness and Injury Science in 2013, volume 3, issue 2, pages 130–142. 4. Stanke C, Kerac M, Prudhomme C, Medlock J, and Murray V systematically reviewed the health effects of drought, with their findings published in PLoS Currents, version 1, under the identifier 7a2cee9e980f91ad7697b570bcc4b004. The article was accessed on February 14, 2021. 5. A fact sheet titled Floods and Health: Fact Sheets for Health Professionals was accessed in PDF format on February 2, 2021. 6. A quantitative risk assessment report on the effects of climate change on selected causes of death in the 2030s and 2050s was accessed in PDF format on February 2, 2021. 7. Wilhite DA, Sivakumar MVK, and Pulwarty R discussed managing drought risk in a changing climate and the role of national drought policy in their article published in Weather and Climate Extremes in 2014, volume 3, pages 4–13. 8. A document titled Natural Hazards: Public Health Considerations was accessed in PDF format on February 2, 2021. 9. Guidance on the development of warning systems for heatwaves and health was accessed in PDF format on February 2, 2021. 10. McMichael AJ explored the relationship between extreme weather events and infectious disease outbreaks in an article published in Virulence in 2015, volume 6, issue 6, pages 543–547. 11. Seltenrich N examined the health effects of heat and cold in an article titled Between Extremes, published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2015, volume 123, issue 11, pages A275–A279. 12. Lu L and Gong P synthesized research findings on climate change and human infectious diseases from global and spatio-temporal perspectives, published in Environmental International. The article was accessed on February 2, 2021. 13. Añel JA, Fernández-González M, Labandeira X, López-Otero X, and De la Torre L analyzed the impact of cold waves and heatwaves on the energy production sector in their study, accessed on February 2, 2021. 14. Xu R, Yu P, Abramson MJ, Johnston FH, Samet JH, Bell ML, and colleagues reviewed the effects of wildfires, global climate change, and human health in an article published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2020, volume 383, pages 2173–2181. 15. Roa L, Velin L, Tudravu J, McClain CD, Bernstein A, and Meara JG discussed the challenges and opportunities of scaling up surgical, obstetric, and anesthesia care globally in the context of climate change in an article published in The Lancet Planetary Health in 2020, volume 4, pages e538–e543. 16. A report titled The Effects of Cold Temperatures on Health was published by the Government of Quebec, Canada, and accessed on February 2, 2021. 17. A document titled Safe Hospitals: Prepared for Emergencies and Disasters was published as part of the Disaster Risk Management for Health Fact Sheets by the Global Platform in May 2011 and accessed on February 2, 2021. 18. Guenther R and Balbus J authored a best practices document titled Primary Protection: Enhancing Health Care Resiliency for a Changing Climate, under the HHS Sustainable and Climate Resilient Health Care Facilities Initiative. The document was accessed on February 2, 2021. 19. A report titled Healthy, Resilient, and Sustainable Communities After Disasters: Strategies, Opportunities, and Planning for Recovery was accessed in PDF format on February 2, 2021. 20. Curtis S, Fair A, Wistow J, Val DV, and Oven K examined the impact of extreme weather events and climate change on health and social care systems in an article published in Environmental Health. The article was accessed on February 2, 2021. 21. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a guideline titled Communicating Risk in Public Health Emergencies: A WHO Guideline for Emergency Risk Communication (ERC) Policy and Practice, accessed on February 2, 2021. 22. The Smart Hospital Toolkit, a practical guide for hospital administrators, health disaster coordinators, health facility designers, engineers, and maintenance staff, was published by the Pan American Health Organization in 2017. It provides strategies for achieving smart health facilities by conserving resources, cutting costs, increasing operational efficiency, and reducing carbon emissions. The document was accessed on February 2, 2021. 23. Moulton AD and Schramm PJ proposed a comprehensive strategy for climate change and public health surveillance in an article published in the Journal of Public Health Management and Practice in 2017, volume 23, issue 6, pages 618–626. 24. A document titled Food and Water Safety During Power Outages and Floods was accessed on February 2, 2021. 25. A report titled Sea-Level Rise, Climate Change, and Health was accessed in PDF format on February 2, 2021. 26. Siebentritt M authored a manual titled Understanding Sea-Level Rise and Climate Change, and Associated Impacts on the Coastal Zone, published as the CoastAdapt Information Manual 2. The document was accessed on February 2, 2021. 27. Hagenlocher M, Meza I, Anderson CC, Min A, Renaud FG, Walz Y, and colleagues reviewed drought vulnerability and risk assessments, identifying persistent gaps and proposing a research agenda in an article published in Environmental Research Letters. The document was accessed on February 2, 2021. 28. Cherng ST, Cangemi I, Trostle JA, Remais J, and Eisenberg JNS explored the relationship between social cohesion, passive adaptation, climate change, and disease in an article published in Global Environmental Change. The article was accessed on February 2, 2021. 29. Matthies F, Bickler G, Marin NC, and Hales S edited a guidance document titled Heat-Health Action Plans, which was accessed on February 2, 2021. 30. A WHO publication titled Public Health Advice on Preventing Health Effects of Heat: New and Updated Information for Different Audiences was accessed on February 2, 2021. 31. Abat C, Chaudet H, Rolain J-M, Colson P, and Raoult D reviewed traditional and syndromic surveillance of infectious diseases and pathogens in an article published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2016, volume 48, pages 22–28. 32. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) published a fact sheet titled Wildfire Smoke: Protect Yourself from Ash in 2018, which was accessed on February 2, 2021. 33. The EPA and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) revised a guide for public health officials titled Wildfire Smoke: A Guide for Public Health Officials in 2019, under the identifier EPA-452/R-19-901. The document was accessed on February 2, 2021. 34. The WHO published a Climate and Health Country Profile 2015 – Nepal, which was accessed on February 2, 2021.
